note: Every way stock bitchat iOS and stock bitchat-android disagree when one codec is fed the other's committed vectors (scripts/bitchat-vectors/cross-replay.sh). source = the codec that produced the bytes, target = the codec that read them. op/field are full-match regexes over the neutral ops of scripts/bitchat-vectors/cross.py; cases is a search regex over the vector case name. status mismatch = the target returned different bytes or a different verdict; not_modeled = the target has no way to express or report that field (data it would drop). An entry that stops reproducing fails the run, so a divergence that upstream fixes cannot linger here. SPEC.md section 12 is the prose form of this file.

divergences.reason: Stock iOS re-compresses the decoded payload with Apple's encoder when it rebuilds the signing preimage and when it relays, instead of reusing the received DEFLATE stream.
divergences.consequence: A signed frame whose compressed payload is not Apple's own DEFLATE stream fails signature verification on iOS although the signature is valid, and iOS relays rewritten bytes. That includes ordinary bitchat-android traffic: the JDK compresses at zlib level 6 and Apple at level 5, which emit different streams for some payloads (10_v1_300_a_b33_sig22 is a real Android frame iOS rejects). bitchat-android fixed its side in its #863; the Swift fix is permissionlesstech/bitchat#1805. Bug, iOS side.

divergences.reason: The reference encoders run different zlib levels: java.util.zip.Deflater at its default (6), Apple COMPRESSION_ZLIB at 5. For most payloads the streams coincide; for this one they do not.
divergences.consequence: Encoder difference, not a defect on its own: every receiver inflates both. It becomes the iOS verification bug above whenever the frame is signed.

divergences.reason: Same zlib level difference, seen from the other side: Android re-encoding iOS's fields emits its level-6 stream.
divergences.consequence: None for Android's verifier, which checks the received bytes (its #863).

divergences.reason: iOS AnnouncementPacket keeps no unknown TLVs, so decode then encode drops them; bitchat-android preserves them in order.
divergences.consequence: None on the wire: iOS never re-encodes a received announce (it relays the packet with its payload bytes untouched and verifies the signature over those bytes). Matters only to code that rebuilds an announce from a decoded one.

divergences.reason: 0x07 is iOS's private-group key update (NoisePayloadType.groupKeyUpdate); bitchat-android has no private groups and rejects the type.
divergences.consequence: Feature gap, not a codec bug: private-group key updates (and invites, 0x06) from iOS are dropped by Android, so Android users cannot be in iOS private groups.

divergences.reason: iOS PeerID(publicKey:) hashes any key length; bitchat-android derives a peer id only from a 32-byte Noise key.
divergences.consequence: None for real keys (Noise static keys are always 32 bytes). iOS is more permissive with malformed input.

divergences.reason: Harness coverage, not a divergence: iOS builds fragment payloads inline in BLEOutboundFragmentPlanner and has no standalone encoder to call. The same case's decode op passes on iOS, and iOS planner output is decoded by Android.
divergences.consequence: None.

divergences.reason: bitchat-android's BitchatPacket has no RSR (request-sync response, flag 0x10) field: it ignores the bit on decode and drops it on re-encode.
divergences.consequence: Signatures are unaffected (iOS clears RSR in the preimage). iOS sends sync responses at TTL 0, so Android never relays them; Android's own sync responses carry no RSR bit, so iOS handles them as ordinary TTL-0 packets rather than solicited responses. Not traced end to end through iOS's ingress guard.

divergences.reason: Same gap as the RSR decode entry: Android cannot build a packet with the RSR bit.
divergences.consequence: See the RSR decode entry.

divergences.reason: 0x12 is iOS's vouch payload (transitive verification); bitchat-android does not know the type and rejects it.
divergences.consequence: Feature gap: vouches from iOS are dropped by Android.

divergences.reason: iOS still accepts the legacy file TLV shape (8-byte FILE_SIZE); bitchat-android requires the 4-byte form and rejects the packet.
divergences.consequence: Files from builds that still emit the legacy shape are dropped by Android. Current iOS encodes the 4-byte form.

divergences.reason: bitchat-android requires a FILE_NAME TLV; iOS decodes a file packet carrying content only.
divergences.consequence: No effect with current builds: iOS's media paths (ChatMediaPreparation) always set a file name and MIME type. A sender that omits the name is dropped by Android.

divergences.reason: bitchat-android's BitchatFilePacket constructor requires a file name and a MIME type; iOS can encode a packet without either.
divergences.consequence: Same as the content-only decode entry: harmless while iOS always names files.

divergences.reason: bitchat-android substitutes application/octet-stream for a missing MIME type; iOS keeps it absent.
divergences.consequence: Cosmetic: the receiver shows a generic file type.

divergences.reason: bitchat-android's IdentityAnnouncement has no direct-neighbors (TLV 0x04) or bridge-geohash (TLV 0x06) field: it keeps them as unknown TLVs and does not interpret them.
divergences.consequence: Android does not learn iOS's mesh topology hints or geohash bridge announcements; the announce itself decodes and verifies.

divergences.reason: Sonar's private-message TLV 0x04 is its reply-parent extension, and its decoder skips any TLV it does not know; both stock decoders reject an unknown TLV.
divergences.consequence: Deliberate (SPEC.md §8.2). Sonar never sends 0x04 to a stock peer: the extended encoding is gated on a verified Sonar 0x53 announce.

divergences.reason: Same reply-parent extension and tolerant decoder as the iOS-file entry.
divergences.consequence: Deliberate; never sent to a stock peer.

divergences.reason: Sonar compresses exactly like Apple (zlib level 5) on both platforms; bitchat-android's JDK uses level 6, which differs for this payload.
divergences.consequence: Deliberate: stock bitchat iOS rebuilds signature preimages by re-compressing, so only Apple's stream lets Sonar's signed frames verify there; bitchat-android verifies over the received bytes and accepts either.

divergences.reason: Sonar knows upstream iOS's Noise types (0x06/0x07 groups, 0x08 voice, 0x12 vouch) and decodes them like stock iOS, then drops them; bitchat-android rejects 0x07.
divergences.consequence: None: Sonar implements none of those features and advertises none of their capability bits.

divergences.reason: File TLV 0x05 is Sonar's message-id extension: Sonar keeps it on decode and re-emits it; bitchat-android skips it and re-encodes without it.
divergences.consequence: Deliberate (SPEC.md §8.3); sent to Sonar peers only.

divergences.reason: Sonar derives a peer id from any key length, like stock iOS; bitchat-android only from 32 bytes.
divergences.consequence: None for real Noise keys (always 32 bytes).

divergences.reason: The crate's Packet holds an 8-byte sender id by type; stock iOS will encode a frame from a shorter one.
divergences.consequence: None on the wire: Sonar never builds such a packet, and the crate decodes the frame iOS produced (this case's decode ops agree).
